### Validation and limitations

The strategy retrieved the one likely relevant record screened in during development, PMID 28358542: relative recall was 1/1 (100%) on that development record. Its abstract supports the Bayesian versus maximum-likelihood comparison and small-sample context, but the simulation design is inferred and needs full-text confirmation. There was no independent validation set or benchmark, so recall is not independently estimated.

I tested small-sample, simulation, and comparator blocks as optional concepts. Each would reduce the count, but the small-sample and simulation blocks miss PMID 28358542; the comparator block may miss eligible studies using other estimator comparisons. They remain unrequired. The resulting 12,364 records exceed the standard 10,000-record workload budget; screening capacity was not supplied.

The cutoff is an Entrez-date bound, with no publication-date limit. Counts reflect the live index with entries through 2017-11-29, not a frozen reconstruction of PubMed as it existed on that date. The internal PRESS-structured critique passed; human PRESS peer review by an information specialist is still needed before use.
